problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=-5x+4xy \\ {y}^{′}=9y-2xy\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the predators and $y=y(t)$ represents the prey. Find the nonzero equilibrium of the model.

$(${{field-1}}
$,$
{{field-2}}$)$
worked_solution:
The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-5x+4xy=0 \\ 9y-2xy=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-5x+4xy & =0 \\ x(-5+4y) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x=0$ or $y=\frac{5}{4}.$ We consider both cases separately.

- If $x=0,$ substituting it into the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}9y-2(0)y=0\,⇒\,y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, one equilibrium is $(0,0).$

- If $y=\frac{5}{4},$ substituting it into the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}9y-2xy & =0 \\ y(9-2x) & =0 \\ \frac{5}{4}(9-2x) & =0 \\ 9-2x & =0 \\ x & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, another equilibrium is $(\frac{9}{2},\frac{5}{4}).$

Therefore, the nonzero equilibrium of the model is
$(\frac{9}{2},\frac{5}{4}).$
